content: Cochlear implant may be indicated for 1 or more of the following:

children.content: Adult with ALL of the following:
Intact cochlear nerves confirmed by CT or MRI, or acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma) excision planned and cochlear nerve preservation thought possible
children.question: Has the patient undergone a CT or MRI to confirm intact cochlear nerves, or is there a planned excision of an acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma) with possible cochlear nerve preservation?

children.content: Need for implant, as indicated by 1 or more of the following:
Asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss and ALL of the following:
Hearing loss, unaided, of 70 dB or greater (ie, severe to profound hearing loss) in one ear
children.question: Does the patient have unaided hearing loss of 70 dB or greater in one ear? If yes, left or right?

children.content: Contralateral ear with 31 to 55 dB hearing loss (ie, mild to moderately severe hearing loss), with difference of at least 15 dB in pure-tone averages between ears
children.question: Does the patient have a contralateral ear with 31 to 55 dB hearing loss and a difference of at least 15 dB in pure-tone averages between ears?

children.content: Limited benefit from appropriately fitted hearing aid in ear to be implanted
children.question: Is there documentation in the medical record indicating limited benefit from an appropriately fitted hearing aid in the ear to be implanted?

children.content: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss of greater than 40 dB with limited (eg, best aided word or open-set sentence cognition test at 60% or less, presented at 60 dB) speech perception benefit from hearing aids
children.question: Does the patient have bilateral sensorineural hearing loss of greater than 40 dB with limited speech perception benefit from hearing aids?

children.content: Unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and ALL of the following:
Hearing loss, unaided, of 70 dB or greater (ie, severe to profound hearing loss) in one ear
children.question: Does the patient have unaided hearing loss of 70 dB or greater in one ear? If yes, left or right?

children.content: Contralateral ear hearing loss less than 30 dB (ie, normal or mild hearing loss)
children.question: Does the patient have contralateral ear hearing loss less than 30 dB, indicating normal or mild hearing loss, in the context of unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and the need for a cochlear implant?

children.content: Limited benefit from appropriately fitted hearing aid in ear to be implanted
children.question: Has the patient experienced limited benefit from an appropriately fitted hearing aid in the ear to be implanted?

children.content: Unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and risk for progression (eg, due to bacterial meningitis)
children.question: Does the patient have unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and is at risk for progression due to bacterial meningitis? If yes, left or right?

children.content: No lesions of acoustic nerve or central auditory pathway causing deafness
children.question: Is there evidence in the medical record that the patient has no lesions of the acoustic nerve or central auditory pathway causing deafness?

children.content: Child with ALL of the following:

Cochleovestibular anatomy compatible with cochlear implant placement (ie, no evidence of anomaly that would preclude implant, such as cochlear aplasia, complete labyrinthine aplasia, lack of cochlear nerve), confirmed by CT or MRI, or acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma) excision planned and cochlear nerve preservation thought possible
children.question: Is there evidence in the patient's medical record of cochleovestibular anatomy compatible with cochlear implant placement, confirmed by CT or MRI, or is there a planned excision of acoustic neuroma with possible cochlear nerve preservation?

children.content: Need for implant, as indicated by 1 or more of the following:
Asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss and ALL of the following:
Hearing loss, unaided, of 70 dB or greater (ie, severe to profound hearing loss) in one ear
children.question: Does the patient have unaided hearing loss of 70 dB or greater in one ear?

children.content: Contralateral ear with 31 to 55 dB hearing loss (ie, mild to moderately severe hearing loss), with difference of at least 15 dB in pure-tone averages between ears
children.question: Does the patient have contralateral ear with 31 to 55 dB hearing loss and a difference of at least 15 dB in pure-tone averages between ears?

children.content: Limited benefit from appropriately fitted hearing aid in ear to be implanted
children.question: Does the patient have limited benefit from an appropriately fitted hearing aid in the ear to be implanted?

children.content: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, as indicated by ALL of the following:
Age 9 months or older
children.question: Is there documentation in the medical record that the patient is 9 months or older with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and a need for a cochlear implant?

children.content: Hearing loss with unaided pure-tone average thresholds of 70 dB or greater (ie, severe hearing loss)
children.question: Does the patient have hearing loss with unaided pure-tone average thresholds of 70 dB or greater, indicating severe hearing loss, and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss?

children.content: Three-month to six-month trial of binaural hearing aids documents lack of or minimal improvement (ie, less than appropriate based on age, developmental stage, or cognitive ability) in auditory development.
children.question: Has the patient undergone a three-month to six-month trial of binaural hearing aids with documented lack of or minimal improvement in auditory development?

children.content: Unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and ALL of the following:
Hearing loss, unaided, of 70 dB or greater (ie, severe to profound hearing loss) in one ear
children.question: Does the patient have unaided hearing loss of 70 dB or greater in one ear?

children.content: Contralateral ear with less than 30 dB hearing loss (ie, normal to mild hearing loss), with difference of at least 15 dB in pure-tone averages between ears
children.question: Does the patient have contralateral ear with less than 30 dB hearing loss and a difference of at least 15 dB in pure-tone averages between ears?

children.content: Limited benefit from appropriately fitted hearing aid in ear to be implanted
children.question: Has the patient experienced limited benefit from an appropriately fitted hearing aid in the ear to be implanted?

children.content: Unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and risk for progression (eg, due to bacterial meningitis)
children.question: Does the patient have unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and is there a risk for progression, such as due to bacterial meningitis?

children.content: Family support and motivation to participate in postimplant rehabilitation
children.question: Is there documentation of family support and motivation for the child to participate in postimplant rehabilitation in the medical record?

children.content: Minimal speech perception 30% or less or lack of developmentally appropriate auditory milestones measured using parent report scales
children.question: Is there documentation in the medical record indicating that the child has minimal speech perception of 30% or less or lacks developmentally appropriate auditory milestones?

children.content: No evidence of central auditory dysfunction (eg, cortical deafness)
children.question: Is there documentation in the medical record indicating no evidence of central auditory dysfunction, such as cortical deafness, in a child?

children.content: Replacement of existing cochlear implant or component (eg, headset/headpiece, microphone, transmitting coil or cable, external speech processor or controller, battery) needed
children.question: Is there documentation in the medical record indicating the need for replacement of an existing cochlear implant or its components such as headset, microphone, transmitting coil, cable, external speech processor, controller, or battery?
